items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-11-01
items.q: they had a grand piano for Purnell.

ctx.x: Could you describe the setup at the... this was at the Beverly Capitol? Mm-hmm. The setup there, the atmosphere, clientele, prices, the way the band was received, general atmosphere of the... of the club and so on.

It was strictly at over 21 places. Strictly cocktail, there was a little Chinese restaurant next door. Um... As you looked at the stage, the... they had a grand piano for Purnell. And he... as you looked at the... well... as you looked at the stage, he was on the right. The banjo was just in front of him, slightly to the left. And then going across the front of the stage was George Lewis, uh... Kid Howard, and Jim Robinson. Directly in the center behind the band, it was kind of... it was in a corner. You had the…
Uh... what about the, um... was there any dancing?

items.title: Alton Purnell Interview, 1958-08-29
items.q: So I continued playing with Smiley and Joe and then I would, when George Lewis would get jobs or something like that they would hire me.

ctx.x: He's back in town now. He's back in town now? Yeah.

Well I worked with Isaiah oh two, three years. And I never would come home with any money. We used to play percentage jobs. When we were on a trip some of the jobs were percentage. Some of them were paid jobs and different things. But as far as I got the money I wanted to have plenty for it and I'd spend it. But anyhow I got a lot of band experience with Isaiah. And then after I left Isaiah's band I began to get a little trios. And my singing helped me out most because I never could play too much solo work. And I…
could do. You were playing with a different key than the rest of the band. That's right, with the rest of the band. You could raise up the pitch.

items.title: Alton Purnell Interview, 1968-03-03
items.q: See, Bunk hired the George Lewis band, which we all played together, and he was just a new man in the band.

ctx.x: Well, Bunk Johnson, if I remember correctly, the records I've got of his, he made with Lou Waters up at Hambone Kelly some years ago after they rediscovered Bunk. You know, they found him pitching cotton or something. I don't know what he was doing, but they brought him a new set of teeth and brought him a trumpet, and away we went.

Yeah, this is the time, around the time I played him, but we were in New York, but we played in 1945, and we made a lot of records while we were there that were very good records. And it's too bad, I mean, Bunk had to pass away, you know, because this was my first chance to do any kind of traveling outside of the South by playing along with Bunk. See, Bunk hired the George Lewis band, which we all played together, and he was just a new man in the band. And so when Bunk came in and accepted our band to play with…
Yeah, boy, it could play an awful lot of instrument, that fella.

items.title: George Lewis Interview, 1968-12-09
items.q: Some of them was playing, some of the fellas didn't even know. You see? Cause you'd take, like... Piano player. Elder Poinnelly.

ctx.x: I know I won't have any church after that. After, uh... The funeral, uh... Good morning. But, uh... He accepted it. And that was the first time he had ever been done. Uh... On Easter Sunday mornings, a big... Uh... Uh... They accepted it again.
Everybody accepted it. And, uh... Some of them was playing, some of the fellas didn't even know. You see? Cause you'd take, like... Piano player. Elder Poinnelly.

Not used to playing hymns. Uh... You got a Lawrence. Uh... Banjo. Uh... for the congregation of the church. And then I met on my last mother that died and I changed my pastoral instance and I met some nuns. We call them sisters, y'all. We call them sisters. Two of them had a youth period of the church. I lived there with Doug, Plotty Jack and some of them. And then I was going to go to Europe. These two young people invited me to come to the church. And then they would come to get me. So, sure enough, they came…
